seated-pelvic-clock-exploration.description: A seated fitted-reference pelvis and spine motion; project-authored, not measured.

supported-seated-side-reach.description: A supported seated side-reach anatomical study; project-authored, not measured.

pause-before-standing.description: A seated pause and whole-torso incline; it stops before claiming to reproduce standing.

mountain-arm-sweep-study.description: A symmetrical standing arm sweep on the fitted reference.

warrior-two-study.description: A frontal wide-stance Warrior II anatomical estimate.

triangle-study.description: A frontal wide-stance triangle anatomical estimate.

chair-pose-study.description: A sagittal hip-and-knee flexion anatomical estimate.

standing-forward-fold-study.description: A sagittal hip-hinge and segmented forward-fold anatomical estimate.

dynamic-chair-clock-study.description: A seated pelvic side-shift anatomical estimate.

shoulder-clock-study.description: A seated left-scapula clock-path anatomical estimate.

sliding-hand-study.description: A seated hand-slide and rib-response anatomical estimate.

seated-counterturn-study.description: A seated pelvis, ribs, and head counter-turn anatomical estimate.

seated-weight-shift-study.description: A seated bilateral weight-shift anatomical estimate.

ankle-flexion-study.description: One ankle alternates between lifting the forefoot and pointing it, with the shin held steady. Project-authored anatomical estimate, not measured motion.

ankle-circle-study.description: The left foot follows a small loop combining forefoot lift, tilt, and return. Project-authored anatomical estimate, not measured motion.

foot-edge-tilt-study.description: A small ankle tilt turns the sole inward and outward while the knee keeps its direction. Project-authored anatomical estimate, not measured motion.

wrist-flexion-study.description: With the elbow bent, one hand changes its angle relative to the forearm. Project-authored anatomical estimate, not measured motion.

wrist-clock-study.description: A supported-arm reference combines two small wrist angles into a hand loop. Project-authored anatomical estimate, not measured motion.

elbow-fold-study.description: The left forearm folds toward the upper arm and opens again while the shoulder stays quiet. Project-authored anatomical estimate, not measured motion.

shoulder-glide-study.description: Both shoulder blades travel forward and back with a small collarbone response. Project-authored anatomical estimate, not measured motion.

forward-arm-reach-study.description: One arm reaches forward, then the upper chest contributes a small following turn. Project-authored anatomical estimate, not measured motion.

head-nod-study.description: The skull nods and returns around its articulation with the upper neck. Project-authored anatomical estimate, not measured motion.

head-sidebend-study.description: The head and upper neck incline toward each shoulder in a small alternating arc. Project-authored anatomical estimate, not measured motion.

spinal-round-arch-study.description: The seated spine rounds and lengthens through the lumbar, thoracic, and neck regions. Project-authored anatomical estimate, not measured motion.

supine-knee-tilt-study.description: With both knees bent, the thighs incline together toward one side and then the other. Project-authored anatomical estimate, not measured motion.

heel-slide-study.description: One bent leg lengthens toward a straight position, then folds back toward its starting shape. Project-authored anatomical estimate, not measured motion.

diagonal-lengthening-study.description: A long leg and the opposite arm move away from the torso, then soften toward the starting position. Project-authored anatomical estimate, not measured motion.

seated-knee-extension-study.description: One shin swings forward as the knee opens; the ankle adjusts to keep the toes facing forward. Project-authored anatomical estimate, not measured motion.

tree-pose-study.description: One leg bends and opens outward while the other remains long beneath the upright trunk. Project-authored anatomical estimate, not measured motion.

warrior-one-study.description: A split stance combines front-leg flexion, back-leg extension, and an overhead arm line. Project-authored anatomical estimate, not measured motion.

extended-side-angle-study.description: A wide stance and one bent knee support an inclined trunk with the upper arm extending overhead. Project-authored anatomical estimate, not measured motion.

wide-standing-fold-study.description: Both hips hinge with the legs spread apart and the arms descending toward the floor. Project-authored anatomical estimate, not measured motion.

pyramid-pose-study.description: The trunk inclines over the front leg in a short split stance with both knees long. Project-authored anatomical estimate, not measured motion.

half-moon-study.description: The pelvis turns sideways as one leg stays beneath it and the other extends outward. Project-authored anatomical estimate, not measured motion.

eagle-arms-study.description: Bent arms move forward and across the chest to show the shoulder and elbow arrangement. Project-authored anatomical estimate, not measured motion.

cow-face-arms-study.description: One elbow points upward while the opposite arm turns behind the trunk. Project-authored anatomical estimate, not measured motion.

prayer-position-study.description: Both elbows bend as the forearms approach the front of the chest. Project-authored anatomical estimate, not measured motion.

upward-prayer-study.description: Both arms elevate and approach one another above the head. Project-authored anatomical estimate, not measured motion.

chair-twist-study.description: The chest and head turn relative to the pelvis while the seated legs stay forward. Project-authored anatomical estimate, not measured motion.

staff-pose-study.description: A long sitting reference moves from slightly bent knees toward two extended legs. Project-authored anatomical estimate, not measured motion.

seated-forward-fold-study.description: From long sitting, the pelvis and spine incline toward the extended legs. Project-authored anatomical estimate, not measured motion.

wide-seated-angle-study.description: Both legs open from long sitting and the torso makes a small forward incline between them. Project-authored anatomical estimate, not measured motion.

legs-up-wall-study.description: A back-lying reference raises both legs while the head and trunk remain horizontal. Project-authored anatomical estimate, not measured motion.
